what_it_does: This paper describes a chip component that converts tiny physical capacitance measurements (capacitance is how much electrical charge you can store) into digital numbers for IoT environmental sensors like humidity and pressure gauges. The challenge is that these measurements are very small and very noisy—quantum thermal noise and manufacturing imperfections corrupt the signal. The solution uses a technique called delta-sigma modulation, which is like taking many rough measurements and mathematically combining them to get a very accurate result. The new design works in continuous time rather than using a clock to sample the signal, which avoids timing jitter and runs more efficiently.
